subject: Post-call recap + model-fit benchmarks / next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@clarityai.com>, Olivia Zhang <olivia.zhang@clarityai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + model-fit benchmarks / next steps

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — great to meet you both. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side: 

- What we heard: primary use case is document summarization at ~1k avg tokens, strict latency targets (~200ms p95), and sensitivity around data residency and audit logs.
- Suggested models to evaluate initially: Mistral-7B-instruct (quantized), Llama-2-13B-8bit, and a Redwood-verified LLM-optimized variant (rwd-13b-v1).
- Next steps: we will run a quick benchmark on your representative prompt set and share Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS and latency percentiles) + quality evals.

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.csv (sample prompts you shared on the call).

Can you confirm the three representative prompt categories are still: extraction, abstractive summary, and instruction-following? If anything changed, please send the updated sample.

I'll follow up with the benchmark links and a short note on quality tradeoffs later today.

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@clarityai.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Zhang <olivia.zhang@clarityai.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + model-fit benchmarks / next steps

Thanks Alex — confirm the three categories are correct. A couple quick clarifications before you run the bench:

- For latency targets, our SLA target is 200ms p95 and we care about p50/p95/p99. Can you include those percentiles?
- For TPS, what baseline should we expect for a single dedicated instance vs. hosted multi-tenant? We are trying to size for ~200 concurrent users at peak (roughly ~20 TPS).
- Also want to flag quality regression sensitivity — if a quantized variant drops Rouge or semantic similarity by >2 points, we need a rollback plan.

If you can include the latency percentiles and per-model quality delta vs. our baseline, that would be ideal.

Sam
Sam Patel
Head of ML Ops, ClarityAI
sam.patel@clarityai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@clarityai.com>, Olivia Zhang <olivia.zhang@clarityai.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + model-fit benchmarks / next steps

Hi Sam / Olivia — looping in the benchmarking notes and the Redwood-verified performance profiles. Please see the short summary below and the attached PDF (redwood_benchmark_report_20260328.pdf) for full results and plots. Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-example-benchmarks

Summary (benchmark run on representative prompt_set_v1.csv):
- Candidate models evaluated: rwd-13b-v1 (default FP16), rwd-13b-8q (8-bit quantized), llm-13b-8bit, mistral-7b-instruct-8q.
- Throughput (single host, dedicated NVIDIA A100): rwd-13b-v1 = 35 TPS, rwd-13b-8q = 48 TPS, llm-13b-8bit = 44 TPS, mistral-7b-instruct-8q = 60 TPS.
- Latency percentiles (p50 / p95 / p99, end-to-end request including tokenization):
  - rwd-13b-v1: 85ms / 185ms / 320ms
  - rwd-13b-8q: 70ms / 165ms / 290ms
  - llm-13b-8bit: 75ms / 170ms / 300ms
  - mistral-7b-instruct-8q: 60ms / 140ms / 240ms

Quality notes (automatic evals vs. your baseline_run_v2):
- rwd-13b-v1: delta Rouge-L = +0.8, semantic-similarity = +0.5
- rwd-13b-8q: delta Rouge-L = -0.9, semantic-similarity = -0.7
- llm-13b-8bit: delta Rouge-L = -0.6, semantic-similarity = -0.4
- mistral-7b-instruct-8q: delta Rouge-L = -1.4, semantic-similarity = -1.1

Recommendation: Based on your latency SLO (200ms p95) and quality sensitivity, we recommend starting with rwd-13b-v1 (FP16) in Dedicated mode for the initial pilot to minimize regression risk, and run an A/B canary of rwd-13b-8q (quantized) against a slice of traffic to measure real-world quality and cost savings. The quantized variant meets your latency target comfortably but shows a measurable quality delta in automated evals — we typically accept ~1.0 delta but will treat >1.0 as a red flag for rollout.

Operational notes and links: 
- Full benchmark PDF (attached) shows per-sequence latency distributions and batch-size sensitivity.
- We uploaded raw evals and prompt sets to Drive (link above).
- HubSpot deal with benchmark summary: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567/DEAL-7892
- Suggested next step: 30-min follow-up next Wed to review canary rollout plan and SLA options.

Let us know which time works and we can send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solution Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0112

We can do the follow-up on Wed at 11am PT. Also please include a short checklist for the canary (metrics to monitor, rollback thresholds, required telemetry). If you can add a short note about audit log retention options and key management for the Dedicated deployment that would be great.

I'll accept the invite once received.

Olivia
